rationale: The flow-versus-stock composition gap is a genuinely new within-firm construct not present in the archive, but the soft-investment share has a denominator (capx + aqc + Δintan) that can approach or cross zero when intangibles amortize down, producing sign flips and unstable ranks that could easily dominate the economics, so it should be winsorized or floored before testing.

The expression is high whenever headcount falls sharply — i.e., for restructuring/downsizing firms — which is the opposite of the "substituting fixed capital for labor and raising operating leverage" story, and once decomposed it is close to the archive's growth-minus-employment-growth family paired with the same NEG(GP/AT) conditioner.

The stated diagnosis is wrong — RANK is invariant to monotone transforms so right-skew in intan/sale cannot explain the weak slope, and the zero mass in intangibles produces identical ties under the bounded share — leaving this as a cosmetic denominator swap on Liquidity_Drain_At_Soft_Asset_Firms.

This is a mechanical equal-weight merger of two already-evaluated signals sharing the identical conditioner; it may modestly improve reliability but adds no new economic content and its result is largely predictable from the two parents.

Debt maturity structure is a legitimately untested dimension here with a coherent rollover-risk mechanism, but scaling goodwill by ceq means the most fragile firms (negative or near-zero book equity) receive large negative or explosive values that invert the intended ranking, so the conditioner should be scaled by assets or the sample cleaned of ceq ≤ 0.

This is a single-conditioner swap on the archive's flagship Acquired_Intangible_Heavy_Base_Low_Gross_Profitability, and the substituted leg (raw, non-industry-adjusted sales per employee) is one of the most industry-determined ratios in accounting data, so the product will largely sort on industry rather than on failed synergy realization.
